title: 7 Influencer Database Options and How to Choose
summary: The right influencer database can help you discover influencers and track meaningful contributions to your brand’s social media presence.
body_markdown:
An influencer database is a centralized system with everything you need to manage the social media creators your brand works with. You can use an influencer search platform, build your own database from publicly available creator information, or use a tool integrated with your ecommerce platform.


According to a[2025 Sprout Social Survey](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/influencer-marketing-statistics/) of 650 marketers, 52% of[business-to-consumer (B2C)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-business-to-consumer-b2c-definition-and-guide) brands partner with 6 to 10 influencers at a time. Another 23% partner with 11 to 19. Managing a roster that big by hand is resource-intensive. Without a good system, promising partnerships might get buried in email threads, campaigns could run without clear performance tracking, and you may keep investing in poor-performing creators.


Here’s what to include in your database, which features are worth looking for, and how to choose a system that matches the size, budget, and goals of your[influencer program](https://www.shopify.com/blog/influencer-program) .


## What is an influencer database?


An influencer database is a searchable, organized collection of social media creators you can use to discover, evaluate, contact, and manage potential partners.


An influencer database typically contains information such as creator contact details, niche, location, audience data, gifting history,[affiliate links](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-make-affiliate-links) , commissions, past campaigns, influencer analytics, and payment terms.


Broadly, these tools fall into two categories:


-


**Influencer discovery tools.** These primarily help you find and shortlist relevant influencers through search and filters. For example,[Modash](https://apps.shopify.com/modash) is built around a large creator database that brands can search using criteria such as platform, location, audience demographics, follower count, and engagement rate.


-


**End-to-end platforms.** These go beyond helping you find influencers to also help with outreach, gifting, affiliate tracking, campaign management, and performance measurement.[GRIN](https://apps.shopify.com/influencer-marketing-for-shopify-by-grin) , for example, combines creator discovery with tools for managing relationships, product seeding, campaigns, affiliate programs, payments, and reporting.

## Factors to consider when choosing an influencer database


- The size of your creator pool
- The specificity of your niche
- Your relationship management needs
- Ecommerce integration requirements
- Ability to scale with your business


There’s no single best influencer discovery platform for every brand. The right choice depends on what you’re trying to accomplish and the complexity of your program. Here are factors to keep in mind as you set out to hire influencers:


### The size of your creator pool


Do you primarily need to find new creators or manage existing relationships with vetted influencers? If you’re launching your first influencer campaign and have 20 prospective creators, a spreadsheet and native social media search tools may be enough. Create columns for each creator’s name, handle, platform, niche, location, audience size, contact information, outreach status, products gifted, and notes.


Amy Liu, founder and CEO of[Tower 28 Beauty](https://www.tower28beauty.com/) , worked with her team to go through YouTube creators’ accounts one by one when she first started her company. “We would write these lists together based on who they followed, who I followed, and then we would just send them products,” she said on[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/tower28-beauty-building-credibility-in-business) .


### The specificity of your niche


Distinguish database size from database relevance; access to millions of influencer profiles sounds impressive, but it provides little value if you can’t efficiently narrow them to the people likely to reach your[target audience](https://www.shopify.com/blog/target-audience) . A good influencer search tool lets you narrow results according to characteristics relevant to your campaign.


Depending on the platform, those filters might include niche (e.g., beauty, fitness, or travel), keyword (e.g., “vegan skincare” or “trail running”), social media platform, creator location, and audience size. For example,[Shopify Collabs](https://collabs.shopify.com/) lets you search influencers within your creator database using keywords and filter creators by niche, engagement rate, location, social account, and audience size. Supported social account filters include Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, Twitch, and X.


### Your relationship management needs


Once you’re running several influencer marketing campaigns simultaneously, discovery may become only a small part of the job. You need a way to remember what you’ve contacted them about, when they responded, and how they’d like to work with you. Useful relationship data might include the date of your last outreach, previous campaign participation, products gifted, negotiations, affiliate offers, and internal notes.


Centralizing this information becomes especially useful when multiple team members manage influencer outreach. Ask whether you need a database that also helps manage communication tasks like product gifting and follow-up communication. An integrated platform, while it may cost more than a basic search tool, could replace several manual workflows.


### Ecommerce integration requirements


If your goals include maximizing conversions and sales, consider whether the influencer database you’re looking at integrates influencer discovery with your existing ecommerce workflows. That can include product gifting, unique[discount codes](https://www.shopify.com/blog/discounts-and-coupons) , affiliate links, sales attribution, commission management, and creator payments.


For example, Shopify Collabs combines many of these tasks with Shopify. You can recruit creators, send gifts and discount codes, create affiliate programs, track affiliate sales and commissions, and automate commission payments.


### Ability to scale with your business


An influencer database becomes more valuable the more you use it. At first, it may simply tell you who a creator is and how to contact them. After several campaigns, it can tell you which creators respond to outreach, who creates useful content, whose audiences convert, what commission structures work, and which relationships are worth renewing.


For the best results, keep that information up to date; record the outcome of outreach and make notes about what worked. Over time, you’ll build a proprietary picture of what an ideal influencer looks like for your business, and your next search can start from your own results rather than from generic top-influencer lists.


## Influencer databases to consider


- Shopify Collabs
- ShopMy
- GRIN
- CreatorIQ
- Upfluence
- Aspire
- Modash


Influencer databases range from free affiliate management tools to specialized platforms for global brands managing campaigns. Some emphasize discovery and audience analysis, while others focus on gifting, sales tracking, and relationship management. Here are seven options to consider, along with their distinguishing features and pricing:


### Shopify Collabs


[Shopify Collabs](https://apps.shopify.com/collabs) is a free influencer search tool that connects influencer partnerships directly to your Shopify store. You can invite creators to join an affiliate program, accept applications through a branded page, send products as gifts, and track sales generated through affiliate links or discount codes.


Its main advantage is that creator commissions and sales attribution are managed within Shopify, making it useful for existing Shopify account holders who want to build an affiliate program without adding a separate platform.


**Pricing:** Free to install for eligible Shopify stores; a 2.9% processing fee on automatic commission payments may apply.


### ShopMy


[ShopMy](https://shopmy.us/home/brands/discover) has a curated network with more than 300,000 creators. Brands can filter potential partners using audience characteristics, location, and actual sales performance. ShopMy also supports product gifting, direct messaging, affiliate commissions, and performance reporting.


**Pricing:** Contact ShopMy for a quote.


### GRIN


[GRIN](https://grin.co/) combines creator discovery with tools for running ongoing influencer programs. GRIN is useful for brands managing multiple creator partnerships because Gia, its in-house AI agent, can prepare personalized outreach, coordinate product gifting, and track campaign deliverables. It can also generate performance reports, reducing the amount of administrative work required from you or your marketing team.


**Pricing:** GRIN has a free plan with creator relationship management, affiliate tracking, and 50 monthly usage credits. Paid plans start at $200 per month and add AI-powered workflow automation and larger credit allowances.


### CreatorIQ


[CreatorIQ](https://www.creatoriq.com/) is designed for larger businesses that manage influencer campaigns across multiple brands or regions. Teams can maintain a shared database of creator contact information, previous collaborations, contracts, and campaign results while controlling which employees can access or edit that information.


CreatorIQ also connects with platforms such as Shopify and TikTok and has an API for sharing influencer data with other business systems. It’s useful for companies whose regional marketing teams run separate campaigns with local influencers but need to compare results across the organization.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing available upon request.


### Upfluence


[Upfluence](https://www.upfluence.com/) ’s Shopify integration can help store owners identify influential people already in their customer base, then recruit them for partnerships. It has product gifting and discount code generation workflows as well. Upfluence emphasizes its relevance for businesses interested in turning existing customers into[brand advocates](https://www.shopify.com/blog/brand-advocacy) .


**Pricing:** Custom quotes based on selected modules, team size, and program volume; a 12-month minimum contract applies.


### Aspire


[Aspire](https://www.aspire.io/) has two approaches to creator recruitment: Brands can search its influencer database or publish opportunities through its Creator Marketplace and receive applications. This combination is useful for brands who want interested creators to come to them rather than relying entirely on outbound outreach. Once you recruit your creators, you can use Aspire to send campaign instructions, review content before publication, and arrange payments.


**Pricing:** Contact Aspire for platform pricing.


### Modash


[Modash](https://www.modash.io/) places particular emphasis on creator discovery and audience evaluation. Its searchable database includes more than 380 million creator profiles, with filters for audience demographics, location, engagement, and other characteristics. It also supports creator relationship management and campaign tracking, making it useful for brands who need detailed search capabilities alongside tools for managing partnerships.


**Pricing:** Plans start at $299 per month with monthly billing, or $199 per month when billed annually.


## Influencer database FAQ


### How do I find an influencer database?


You can use an influencer search platform, build your own database from publicly available creator information, or use a tool integrated with your ecommerce platform. Shopify sellers can use Shopify Collabs to search its existing creator database and manage creators they recruit through direct invitations or applications.


### Can I create my own influencer database?


Yes, a spreadsheet can work well for a small influencer marketing program and costs little or nothing to maintain. As your influencer outreach grows, you can migrate that information to a dedicated platform if manual updates, gifting, attribution, or social media management for campaigns become too time-consuming.


### What are some of the most popular influencer databases?


Popular influencer databases and creator marketing platforms include Shopify Collabs, ShopMy, GRIN, CreatorIQ, Upfluence, Aspire, and Modash. The right option depends on the size of your influencer program and whether you primarily need a discovery tool or a platform for managing creator relationships from recruitment through sales attribution.
